chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the two parties from the people of falsehood who meet in battle, can I sell them the weapons? He (peace be upon him) said: Sell them what is defensive for them, like the armor and the shoes, and items such as these.
ai.seo_question: Can I sell weapons to both sides in a battle between non-Muslims?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition on selling weapons to 'ahl al-batil' applies primarily to offensive arms used for fighting, while defensive gear such as armor and footwear remains permissible for trade with both sides. This distinction highlights the practical legal nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the economic aspects of conflict, ensuring that essential protective items are not restricted even when sold to opposing non-Muslim factions.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Muhammad Bin Qays who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the two parties from the people of the falsehood who meet in battle, can I sell the weapons to these two?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You can sell to both of them what is defensive for them, like the armours, and the shoes, and (items) such as these’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the two groups of falsehood who fight each other; if I can sell arms to them.
He (the Imam) said, ‘You can sell to them protective materials, like shields and shoes and so on.’”
